title: Director, External Scouting
location: Cambridge, Massachusetts, United States of America
description:
Introduction to Role

AstraZeneca is building a more connected, end-to-end approach to academic collaboration across BioPharma R&D. As Director, External Scouting, you will shape how we identify, assess and advance external science and collaboration opportunities that can influence our portfolio, strengthen future capabilities and accelerate scientific innovation.

You will combine enterprise-level strategic leadership with hands-on accountability for delivery. Working as a trusted partner to Academic Alliances leadership and senior therapeutic area leaders, you will set and prioritize the scouting agenda, interpret emerging science and ecosystem shifts, and determine how external innovation approaches such as Target Innovation, preclinical molecule collaborations, CoSolve and public-private partnerships, including IHI, can create the greatest strategic value.

You will also help evolve how external scouting is delivered, using AI, automation, structured data and scalable workflows to improve the speed, consistency and quality of decision-making while ensuring scientific and strategic judgement remains at the center.


Why This Role

This is an opportunity to define where AstraZeneca engages with external science and turn that strategy into tangible outcomes. You will lead high-impact opportunities, build relationships with influential academic and scientific partners, and create scalable approaches that expand the reach and effectiveness of the Academic Alliances team.

Your impact will extend beyond individual searches or partnerships. You will help build a repeatable, enterprise-level scouting capability that gives senior leaders earlier access to emerging science, qualified opportunities and decision-ready insights.

Based in Cambridge, US, this role includes regular in-person engagement with AstraZeneca teams and external partners across multiple locations.


Accountabilities

Set and prioritize external scouting strategy

  • Partner with senior leaders to identify high-impact scientific opportunities, portfolio uncertainties and future capability gaps.
  • Anticipate external developments that could challenge AstraZeneca assumptions, priorities or competitive positioning, including emerging needs that have not yet become formal scouting requests.
  • Set priorities across therapeutic areas and scientific domains, making clear choices about where relationship capital, team capacity and collaboration investment can create the greatest value.
  • Translate scientific and external ecosystem signals into strategic options and recommendations that influence portfolio direction, capability decisions and future partnering activity.

Own strategic direction and delivery

  • Take accountability for the quality, pace and outcomes of the external scouting portfolio, from the initial scientific question through opportunity assessment, decision-making and transition to the appropriate collaboration owner.
  • Personally lead selected high-stakes, ambiguous or enterprise-critical searches where senior scientific judgement, external credibility or rapid problem-solving can add unique value.
  • Enable colleagues to lead defined searches and opportunity assessments by establishing outcomes, decision criteria, guardrails and review points while retaining accountability for final recommendations.
  • Mobilize expertise across scientific functions, strategy, Business Development, Legal, data and alliance management to advance opportunities through diligence and governance and support seamless transition to the Academic Partnerships team.
  • Ensure promising opportunities progress toward a clear decision or collaboration pathway, while enabling well-reasoned decisions not to pursue opportunities when appropriate.

Build AI-enabled and scalable scouting capabilities

  • Identify repeatable scouting activities that can be accelerated or strengthened through AI, automation, structured data and standardized workflows.
  • Create, sponsor or oversee AI-enabled tools and processes supporting scientific landscape scanning, opportunity triage, expert and institution identification, evidence synthesis, pipeline visibility and decision preparation.
  • Establish quality standards, validation checks, decision rights and escalation pathways so AI-enabled outputs enhance, rather than replace, scientific and strategic judgement.
  • Embed tools into practical workflows, build capability across the team and evaluate their impact on speed, consistency, insight quality, capacity and stakeholder experience.
  • Apply appropriate human oversight, quality assurance and risk management to AI-enabled analysis and decision support.
  • Use insights from delivery to continuously improve scouting methods, data assets, prompts, templates and operating processes.

Direct the strategic use of external innovation models

  • Determine where Target Innovation, preclinical molecule collaborations, CoSolve, IHI and other external collaboration models can create differentiated value across portfolio priorities.
  • Establish portfolio-level selection criteria, measures of success and governance for these mechanisms.
  • Shape preclinical molecule collaboration strategies, including opportunities where external access to internal assets can test hypotheses, extend scientific reach or create future options.
  • Sponsor Target Innovation and CoSolve challenge portfolios focused on priority scientific or capability gaps, ensuring outputs and learning inform future strategy.
  • Lead or sponsor selected IHI and other public-private partnership opportunities, shaping the value proposition, partner landscape, internal commitment and governance approach.

Create alliances and strengthen strategic ecosystems

  • Identify and shape new academic alliances and multi-party collaborations that address strategic needs beyond a single project or transaction.
  • Serve as a senior relationship owner for priority institutions, academic leaders, ecosystem partners and influential scientific networks.
  • Build durable access to emerging science, talent, technologies and collaboration opportunities within strategically important ecosystems.
  • Represent AstraZeneca externally with credibility and sound judgement, strengthening our position as a thoughtful and reliable scientific partner.
  • Create continuity from early scouting and relationship development through opportunity shaping, partnering decisions and transition to alliance ownership.

What You'll Bring

You bring scientific depth together with strategic judgement and a passion for translating external innovation into meaningful opportunities. You can move comfortably between enterprise strategy and hands-on execution, building credibility with senior executives and leading scientists while mobilizing multidisciplinary teams to deliver results.

You are energized by emerging science, new collaboration models and the opportunity to use AI and data responsibly to improve how scientific opportunities are identified and evaluated. You know when to move quickly, when to challenge assumptions and when additional evidence is needed to make a thoughtful decision.


Essential Skills/Experience

  • MS in life sciences discipline or equivalent depth of scientific, commercial and strategic experience.
  • 10+ years of experience with increasing scope and influence in pharmaceutical, biotechnology, academic research, technology transfer, consulting or another science-led environment.
  • Demonstrated experience setting external scouting, external innovation or collaboration strategy across multiple scientific, therapeutic or portfolio areas.
  • Track record of personally delivering complex scientific scouting and opportunity assessment while also leading delivery through others and maintaining accountability for outcomes.
  • Evidence that externally sourced opportunities, scientific insights or ecosystem intelligence have materially influenced senior-level portfolio, investment, capability or strategic decisions.
  • Proven ability to determine when and how Open Innovation and collaboration mechanisms should be deployed, including making well-supported decisions not to pursue an opportunity.
  • Experience creating or materially shaping academic alliances, consortia, multi-party collaborations or public-private partnerships and building alignment among senior internal and external stakeholders.
  • Experience designing, implementing or sponsoring scalable digital, data or AI-enabled tools and processes that improve scientific, strategic or operational workflows.
  • Ability to establish appropriate human oversight, validation, quality assurance and risk management for AI-enabled analysis and decision support.
  • Established credibility working with senior executives, institutional leaders and leading scientists, with the ability to challenge assumptions respectfully and make sound decisions when evidence is incomplete.
  • Demonstrated leadership of complex cross-functional initiatives and experience developing others through coaching, matrix leadership or formal people leadership.
  • Strong strategic judgement, prioritization, synthesis, negotiation and communication skills, with the executive presence to influence decisions across organizational boundaries.

Desirable Skills/Experience

  • PhD or MD with a minimum of 7 years
  • Experience influencing enterprise-level or multi-therapeutic-area R&D strategy.
  • Experience shaping portfolios of preclinical molecule collaborations, external scientific challenges, target discovery partnerships or related external innovation models.
  • Experience integrating academic scouting with Business Development, portfolio strategy, Open Innovation and alliance management.
  • Practical experience using AI-assisted research, scientific landscaping, evidence synthesis, knowledge management, workflow automation or opportunity-tracking solutions.
  • Experience creating or scaling AI-enabled approaches for landscape scanning, opportunity triage, expert or institution identification, pipeline visibility or decision preparation.
  • Experience developing selection criteria, measures of success or governance for portfolios of external collaborations.
  • Experience representing an organization within prominent scientific ecosystems, institutional leadership forums or senior partnership governance.
  • Experience developing relationships that provide sustained access to emerging science, technologies, scientific talent and future collaboration opportunities.

Why AstraZeneca

Here, courage, curiosity, and collaboration fuel a relentless focus on transforming cancer outcomes, powered by a pipeline that fuses cutting-edge science with advanced technology. You will work in an environment where unexpected teams come together to spark bold ideas, backed by meaningful investment and a clear path from discovery to impact. We value kindness alongside ambition, and we empower leaders at every level to ask sharp questions, take smart risks, and turn data into decisions that help patients sooner.


Compensation & Benefits

The annual base pay for this position ranges from $172,624.00 - $258,936.00. Our positions offer eligibility for various incentives—an opportunity to receive short-term incentive bonuses, equity-based awards for salaried roles and commissions for sales roles. Benefits offered include qualified retirement programs, paid time off (i.e., vacation, holiday, and leaves), as well as health, dental, and vision coverage in accordance with the terms of the applicable plans.


When we put unexpected teams in the same room, we unleash bold thinking with the power to inspire life-changing medicines. In-person working gives us the platform we need to connect, work at pace and challenge perceptions. That's why we work, on average, a minimum of three days per week from the office. But that doesn't mean we're not flexible. We balance the expectation of being in the office while respecting individual flexibility.


Join us in our unique and ambitious world.

In furtherance of that mission, we welcome and consider applications from all qualified candidates, regardless of their protected characteristics. title: E-Payments Analyst
description:
Position Summary

The E-Payments Analyst performs daily processing and support tasks within the E-Payments department at Credit Union of Texas, including ACH, wire transfers, check processing, Remote Deposit Capture (RDC), Zelle, and payroll deduction. Working under moderate supervision in a fast-paced, production-driven environment, the role ensures timely, accurate, and compliant processing of electronic payments while delivering excellent service to members and internal staff. The Analyst applies CUTX-approved AI and analytics tools to support exception research, document triage, and member communications, with human-in-the-loop review on every member-impacting output.

Key Responsibilities

Daily Payment Processing

  • Perform daily processing tasks across E-Payments channels including ACH, wire transfers, check processing, Remote Deposit Capture (RDC)/ATM, Zelle, and payroll deduction, meeting all internal deadlines and service-level goals.
  • Cross training with the Items department learning the Items Processing Operator role.
  • Enter direct payments (ACH external or internal transfers) in a timely manner for member loan and lease payments, and provide guidance to members and staff on these transactions.
  • Process returned items promptly to ensure accurate reversal of payments or deposits, including reversing loan payments, debiting member accounts for returned electronic debits, and handling unpaid check deposits.
  • Monitor transaction queues and address exceptions or errors promptly, escalating to E-Payments management or supervisor when appropriate.

Member & Internal Service

  • Provide outstanding service to internal team members and external members; respond to phone calls and emails related to E-Payments inquiries with professionalism, empathy, and accuracy.
  • Assist members and staff with questions or issues related to payments initiated through Online Banking or Mobile Services; research and resolve issues to ensure member satisfaction.
  • Defuse tense situations and communicate professionally with individuals of varying personalities.
  • Handle confidential and sensitive financial information with discretion at all times.

Balancing, Reconciliation & General Ledger

  • Ensure daily general ledger entries are completed accurately according to established procedures.
  • Review and balance all settlement reports for assigned payment channels.
  • Support E-Payments management in balancing ACH files and identifying outages or discrepancies.

Compliance & Risk

  • Ensure all payment processing activity complies with NACHA Operating Rules, Regulation E, Regulation CC, Regulation J, UCC 4A, BSA/AML, OFAC, and the USA PATRIOT Act as applicable to the role.
  • Identify and escalate any suspicious activity, potential fraud, or compliance concerns immediately to management.
  • Maintain audit-ready documentation for all transactions, exceptions, and member communications.

Collaboration & Continuous Improvement

  • Collaborate with team members to ensure smooth daily operations across the E-Payments function.
  • Maintain a positive, proactive attitude in a fast-paced environment with frequent interruptions.
  • Participate in pilots of CUTX-approved AI tools that support the E-Payments function, contribute feedback, and adopt approved enhancements.
  • Recommend process improvements to management based on patterns observed in daily processing and member inquiries.

Performance Outcomes & KPIs

Outcome

Primary KPI

Reporting Cadence

Target / Direction

Payment transactions are processed accurately and within internal deadlines.

Daily Processing Accuracy Rate — percent of transactions processed without rework or correction.

Monthly

▲ ≥ 99%

Settlement and general ledger entries are balanced daily.

Daily Balancing Completion Rate — percent of business days settlement reports are balanced by cutoff.

Monthly

▲ 100%

Returned items are processed promptly to minimize member and CUTX exposure.

Return Item Turnaround — average business days to process returned items within regulatory windows.

Monthly

▼ Within Reg CC / NACHA timeframes

Members and internal staff receive timely, accurate support.

Inquiry Response Time — average time to respond to E-Payments phone or email inquiries.

Monthly

▼ [Target — confirm with Manager, E-Payments]

Payment files comply with NACHA, Reg E, Reg CC, Reg J, UCC 4A, BSA/AML, and OFAC requirements.

Audit-Ready File Rate — percent of files passing internal compliance review without material exception.

Quarterly

▲ ≥ 98%

AI-augmented outputs supporting payment exception research and member communications are reviewed by the role holder before action.

Human-in-the-Loop Review Rate on AI Outputs — percent of AI-assisted outputs reviewed and either accepted, adjusted, or escalated by the Analyst before action.

Monthly

▲ 100%

Qualifications

Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent required.
  • Associate or bachelor's degree preferred.

Experience

  • Minimum one to two (1–2) years of similar or related experience in payments operations, banking operations, or a closely related field.
  • Previous experience in ACH, wire transfer, or check processing strongly preferred.
  • Prior credit union or community bank experience preferred.
  • Prior experience using AI- or analytics-augmented operations tools preferred.
  • Bilingual English / Spanish preferred.

Licenses, Registrations, and Certifications

  • None required.

Knowledge & Skills

  • Working knowledge of NACHA Operating Rules, Regulation E, Regulation CC, Regulation J, UCC Article 4A, BSA/AML, OFAC, and USA PATRIOT Act requirements as applied to electronic payments.
  • Moderate computer and technology proficiency, including Microsoft Office (Excel, Outlook, Word, Teams) and the ability to learn CUTX's core, online banking, and payment processing platforms.
  • Excellent customer service skills and a genuine desire to help others.
  • Strong multitasking skills, attention to detail, and documentation discipline in a high-volume, deadline-driven environment.
  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to draft clear, accurate member-facing responses.
  • Good judgment and discretion when handling confidential financial information.
  • Ability to work effectively under pressure and remain focused through frequent interruptions.

7. Core Competencies

Competency

Proficiency Level

Why This Matters in This Role

AI Literacy

Intermediate

The role uses AI-augmented exception research, document extraction, and drafting tools (Tier 2) and is responsible for human-in-the-loop review on every member-impacting output.

Member Centricity

Intermediate

The role supports members and staff with payment inquiries that often involve time-sensitive funds; tone, accuracy, and responsiveness directly affect CUTX's reputation.

Operational Discipline

Advanced

Daily deadlines, balancing requirements, and high transaction volume require strict adherence to procedure and accurate documentation on every item.

Compliance Orientation

Advanced

NACHA, Reg E, Reg CC, Reg J, UCC 4A, BSA/AML, and OFAC are applied in daily work; mistakes have direct member, financial, and regulatory impact.

Risk Awareness

Intermediate

Payments processing is a frequent fraud and error vector; the Analyst must identify suspicious patterns and escalate exceptions in real time.

Communication

Intermediate

The role responds to members and internal staff by phone and email and must communicate clearly under pressure and across varied personalities.

AI & Technology Expectations

AI-Augmented Workflows

The following workflows are AI-augmented in this role. The E-Payments Analyst is expected to work fluently within these workflows, exercise sound judgment over AI outputs, and follow all applicable controls.

  • AI-assisted exception research — AI summarizes transaction history and surfaces likely root cause for returned items, rejects, and member inquiries.
  • Document extraction and triage — AI extracts structured fields from RDC images, wire requests, and ACH return notices to support faster processing.
  • AI-assisted drafting of internal and member communications — AI helps draft responses to inquiries, which the Analyst reviews and finalizes before sending.
  • Anomaly and outlier flagging — AI flags transactions outside normal volume, amount, or counterparty patterns for Analyst review.

AI Tier and Human-in-the-Loop Responsibility

This role operates in AI Tier 2 for its principal AI-augmented workflows (see Appendix A). The E-Payments Analyst retains accountability for any decision, communication, or member/employee-impacting action influenced by AI output, consistent with the CUTX Generative AI Usage Policy §3.4.

The E-Payments Analyst is required to:

  • Apply human-in-the-loop review on every AI-assisted exception finding, extracted document field, and drafted member or internal communication before action is taken.
  • Stop reliance on AI output and escalate immediately if the output appears inaccurate, biased, non-compliant, or outside the role's documented scope (Generative AI Usage Policy §3.5).
  • Refrain from entering member non-public personal information (NPI), confidential CUTX information, or material non-public information into any AI tool not explicitly approved for that data classification.
  • Complete all required AI training within thirty (30) days of hire and maintain currency on annual refreshers.

Approved AI Tools

The role is approved to use the following AI tools in performing essential functions (subject to the Generative AI Usage Policy and any tool-specific guidance issued by the AI Council):

  • CUTX-approved internal AI assistants (e.g., Sam) for general productivity and approved knowledge tasks.
  • Microsoft Copilot for office productivity (drafting, summarization, spreadsheet support).
  • CUTX-approved AI-augmented capabilities embedded in the core, online banking, and payment processing platforms.

Use of AI tools outside this list requires prior approval from the role's department leader and the AI Council, per the Generative AI Usage Policy §4.

Prohibited AI Use

In addition to the prohibited uses defined in the Generative AI Usage Policy §3.6, the following are specifically prohibited in this role:

  • Using AI output as the sole basis for any adverse member action, including a decision to reverse a credit, hold funds, return an item, or close access to a payment channel.
  • Entering member NPI (full account numbers, Social Security numbers, member identification documents, wire instructions) into any AI tool not explicitly approved for that data classification.
  • Using consumer AI tools to draft regulatory notices (e.g., Reg E error resolution notices); these must be drafted from approved templates and reviewed per existing procedure.
  • Using AI to make BSA/AML, OFAC, or fraud determinations without documented human review and escalation per policy.

Compliance & Regulatory Responsibilities

Enterprise Compliance Obligations

The E-Payments Analyst is responsible for all enterprise compliance obligations applicable to a CUTX team member, including BSA/AML, OFAC, USA PATRIOT Act/CIP/CDD, GLBA and the Safeguards Rule, Fair Lending laws (ECOA/Reg B, Fair Housing Act), UDAAP, Information Security and Acceptable Use, and the CUTX Code of Conduct.

AI-Specific Compliance Obligations

The E-Payments Analyst is responsible for the CUTX Generative AI Usage Policy (TRAIGA / HB 149-aligned), the CUTX AI Playbook (including Tier 2 obligations applicable to this role), and Texas Responsible Artificial Intelligence Governance Act (TRAIGA / HB 149) requirements applicable to the role.

Role-Specific Compliance Obligations

  • NACHA Operating Rules and Guidelines applicable to ACH origination, receipt, returns, and exceptions.
  • Regulation E (Electronic Fund Transfers) — error resolution, unauthorized transactions, and disclosures.
  • Regulation CC (Availability of Funds and Collection of Checks) — funds availability, holds, and check processing.
  • Regulation J — Fedwire funds transfer rules.
  • Uniform Commercial Code Article 4A — wholesale funds transfers and wire transfer obligations.
  • Bank Secrecy Act / Anti-Money Laundering (BSA/AML) requirements applicable to payments monitoring and reporting.
  • Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC) sanctions screening obligations on payment transactions.
  • USA PATRIOT Act provisions applicable to payments and member identification.
  • CUTX E-Payments, Wire Transfer, ACH, and RDC policies and procedures.

Working Conditions & Physical Requirements

This role is performed on-site at the CUTX Corporate Office in a standard office environment with no hazardous or significantly unpleasant conditions. Essential physical activities include the ability to remain seated at a workstation for extended periods; use fingers, hands, and wrists for repetitive motions such as typing and handling documents; communicate clearly by phone, email, and in person with members, vendors, and internal partners; hear and engage in normal conversations; visually review printed and electronic documents for accuracy; and occasionally stand, walk, stoop, kneel, crouch, or lift and move up to 10 pounds. Reasonable accommodations will be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of this role, consistent with the Americans with Disabilities Act and CUTX policy.

Compliance Requirement

The responsibilities contained within this job description remain compliant with the Bank Secrecy Act/Anti-Money Laundering, Office of Foreign Assets Control, and USA PATRIOT Act as they apply to the duties of the position.

Acknowledgement & Disclaimer

This job description is intended to describe the general nature and level of work being performed by individuals assigned to this position. It is not intended to be an exhaustive list of all responsibilities, duties, and skills required, and CUTX reserves the right to modify, add to, or remove duties at any time as business needs require.

Employment with CUTX is at-will. This job description does not constitute an employment contract.

description:
Why Join PT Solutions?

At PT Solutions Physical Therapy, we’re more than just a private practice—we’re a clinician-founded, mission-driven community dedicated to expanding access to life-changing care. As a Patient Service Coordinator, you’ll be the vital link between patients, providers, and insurers—ensuring every step of the care journey is seamless, efficient, and supportive.

In this role, you’ll take ownership of key administrative and communication processes that keep our practice moving. From verifying insurance coverage and securing prior authorizations to coordinating physician referrals and optimizing schedules, you'll play a central part in helping patients access the care they need—quickly and confidently.

At PT Solutions, we invest in our team with ongoing training, mentorship, and clear paths for advancement. If you're passionate about helping others and ready to grow in a supportive, forward-thinking organization—this is your opportunity.

Your Responsibilities as a Patient Service Coordinator

  • Reconcile patient payments and units billed while following HIPAA guidelines
  • Follow appropriate processes for Insurance Verification and/or benefits management
  • Obtain authorization and/or prior authorization
  • Over the counter collections and reconciliation of all charges weekly and monthly
  • Maintain relationships with patients, providers, clinicians, and internal operational departments

Qualifications

  • At minimum, a High School or GED diploma (Submission of diploma for the highest level of education obtained will be required).
  • 1-2 years of customer service experience (experience with healthcare preferred).
  • Spanish-speaking (preferred)

Schedule

  • Part Time: Tuesday/Thursday/Friday 3:00p-7:00p

Compensation

Pay Range: $18-$21/hour (Any posted pay range considers multiple compensations factors including background, experience, and work location while also allowing for salary growth within the position)

What Else You Can Expect

In addition to medical, dental, vision, a 401K with match and other great benefits, you can also expect to receive:

  • Competitive compensation with ability to earn performance-based incentives
  • Professional development through strategic internal platforms
  • Opportunity for career progression with a nationwide physical therapy practice
  • Paid Time Off (PTO) and either Sick Leave or Extended Illness Bank (EIB) accrual (dependent on state laws)
  • Reimbursement for endurance race entry fees

A Top Workplace

At PT Solutions, we’re more than colleagues; we’re a tight-knit community united in our mission to expand access to quality care. Our commitment to you is evident in our industry-leading professional development opportunities. From ongoing evidence-based clinical education to dedicated mentorship opportunities and an APTA-accredited Orthopedic Residency Program, we propel our clinicians toward excellence in physical therapy, occupational therapy, speech-language pathology, and athletic training.

PT Solutions has been named a 2026 USA Today Top Workplace for the fifth consecutive year, based entirely on employee feedback. We’ve also earned five Culture Excellence Awards for Innovation, Professional Development, Work-Life Flexibility, Appreciation, and Purpose & Values. This recognition reflects a culture built around supporting our people. It’s not just what we do, but how we make people feel. Through human connection, intentional care, and being all in for one another, we create experiences that make a difference. Because together, we do great better.

Let’s go further together and transform care. Join the #PTSLife today! To see what #PTSLife is like, visit Instagram, Facebook, and LinkedIn.

We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome all qualified candidates to apply!

title: Temporary Full-time Ophthalmic Technician
description:
We are seeking a Temporary Full-Time Ophthalmic Technician to join our respected practice, located in Redding, California

This is your chance to build a rewarding career in eye care with a team that values your skills and supports your growth. Enjoy regular hours with no late evenings or major holidays, a comprehensive benefits package, and a collaborative work environment where your contributions truly make a difference.

Ideal candidates will have at least two years of recent experience as an Ophthalmic Technician. COA/COT certification is highly preferred.

Apply today and take the next step in your ophthalmology career!

This is your opportunity to join one of the areas most recognized leaders in ophthalmology and optometry. Shasta Eye Medical Group is an ophthalmic practice with an optical dispensary and affiliated Ambulatory Surgery Center (ASC). This unique and diverse group of doctors provides the most comprehensive vision care in California’s north state region. In addition to providing Comprehensive Ophthalmology, we offer sub specialists in Cornea, External Disease, Uveitis, Refractive Surgery, and Glaucoma. We strive to provide compassionate, comprehensive, state-of-the-art ophthalmic care in the north state region. We are committed to customer service and making every interaction extraordinary while inspiring the complete confidence of our patients. Our employees contribute directly to the growth and success of our practices and take pride in being a member of our team. We strongly believe that the manner in which our patients and customers are treated by our employees is as important as the services provided by the doctor.

All of us at Shasta Eye Medical Group are committed to inclusion and belonging. We believe today more than ever that creating an environment where everyone can bring their authentic selves to work and make it easy for others to do the same will benefit us all. It isn’t speaking the words, but starts with a culture of caring, listening and service. We would thoroughly enjoy meeting with you and discussing our employment opportunities.

The Ophthalmic Technician I will perform a range of duties which include preparing the patient to see Ophthalmologist and/or Optometrist and conduct preliminary exam and captures medical history. In addition, the preparation of examination and treatment rooms, performing basic and routine vision screening examinations, administering eye medications, cleaning, and maintaining ophthalmic instruments and assisting physicians during minor surgical and laser procedures may be required. Traveling to other locations may also be necessary to support clinical needs.

Responsibilities

  • Make introductions and establish rapport with patients
  • Initiate patient evaluation, documenting the chief complaint, history of present illness, review of systems, and all pertinent ocular findings accurately and in accordance with compliance guidelines.
  • Perform pre-exam testing to include visual acuity assessment, including pinhole and glare testing, confrontational visual field testing, assess extra ocular muscles, pupillary evaluation, tonometry, assess angles, pupillary dilation, and all other patient services as requested by the physician including specialty tests such as color vision screening, stereopsis, and dry eye testing
  • Perform lensometry and specialized testing such as visual fields, keratometry, A/B scans, and ophthalmic photography optical coherence tomography (OCT), and optical biometry
  • Additional testing as requested by doctor
  • Perform retinoscopy and refractometry. Assist with minor surgical procedures or laser treatments in the office
  • Assist with fitting contact lenses and instruct patients in care and insertion of lenses
  • Complete requests for prescription refills as authorized by physician, with full documentation in patient chart
  • Educate patients regarding administration of medications and pre- and post-operative instructions as directed by physicians
  • Check temperature of medical refrigerator daily
  • Maintain and conduct inventory of medications and supplies
  • Assist with maintenance of clinical examination equipment
  • Clean surgical instruments in preparation for sterile processing
  • Inspect instruments periodically for damage, send for repair, and request a replacement, as necessary
  • Open and close exam lanes daily, ensuring that equipment is wiped down in an appropriate manner and as per office procedures, battery powered instruments are seated properly in re-charging wells, slit lamps and projectors are switched off under covers
  • Follow all safety procedures as per guidelines
  • Prioritize building and maintaining a positive relationship with doctors and clinical colleagues
  • Executes duties of position in a professional and courteous manner
  • Handles sensitive information in a confidential manner
  • Perform other tasks and duties as assigned

Qualifications

  • High School diploma or equivalent required
  • Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to communicate clearly and effectively with patients, staff, managers, and doctors
  • Basic computer literacy required
  • Highly energetic with a positive attitude
  • Must be willing to travel to other offices occasionally to meet the demands of business
  • Must be able to walk and stand for eight hours
  • Must be able to type or write legibly in a dimly lit setting
  • Certified Ophthalmic Assistant (COA) preferred
  • Certified Ophthalmic Scribe (OSC) preferred
  • Certified Ophthalmic Technician (COT) preferred
  • One to two years’ experience in multi-specialty clinic preferred

In Turn We Will Provide

  • Benefits to full-time team members that include comprehensive medical, dental and optical coverage, 401K and short- and long-term disability
  • Company paid life insurance
  • Paid parking where applicable
  • Paid holidays and generous paid time off
  • Team oriented working environment where you are heard and respected
  • Clear career ladder opportunities
  • Offered pay 23.00/Per Hr.

title: Technician - Digital Delivery - Civil 3D/ Naviswork - Infra/ utilities
description:
Purpose of the role

Produce models and drawings to the project's standards. This is the production core of the team and the largest single grade in it. The role carries one accountability of its own on the responsibility matrix: keeping the drawings as the single source of truth for what is extracted from the model in 2D.

Key responsibilities

What the role is accountable for

· Maintaining the single source of truth for the 2D extraction of the drawings, so that what is issued matches the model it came from.

Production

· Model utility networks, corridors and surfaces in Civil 3D within the assigned scope.

· Deliver models and drawings against the team's plan.

· Apply NOC data standardisation and base plan standardisation.

· Keep base plan and title block requirements correct for the milestone stage.

· Produce BIM model geometry and attributes, and export to the formats required.

Checking

· Produce cut sheets, bind drawings and run the drawing quality control self-check.

· Apply the discipline model checklist, the 3D check.

· Apply the drawing checklist and CAD standard compliance check, the 2D check.

· Take part in the final drawing sanity check before the set goes to review.

Working in the team

· Fix the clashes assigned, and update the model rather than only the drawing.

· Contribute to quantity take-off where it feeds the bill of quantities.

· Report modelling problems and blockers to the senior technician promptly rather than working around them.

Technical requirements

· Civil 3D to a working level: pipe networks, corridors, surfaces and sheet production.

· AutoCAD.

· Awareness of Navisworks and of how clashes are assigned and closed.

· Autodesk Construction Cloud or BIM 360 for filing work in the right place and state.

· Bluebeam Revu for receiving and answering markups.

Qualifications and experience

· Diploma in Civil Engineering or Draughtsmanship.

· Three or more years of infrastructure drafting and modelling.

· Civil 3D used on live projects is essential.

Behaviours we are selecting for

· Follows a standard precisely.

· Asks early when something is unclear.

· Takes correction on a drawing without taking it personally.

How performance is measured

· Output against allocation.

· Turnaround time on markups.

· Checklist compliance when the work is audited.

Assessment against the team competency framework

New joiners at this grade are assessed against the team's nine competency areas during onboarding, each rated Not Yet, Basic, Developing or Competent:

· Understanding project deliverables

· Authority standards and catalogues, for Abu Dhabi, Dubai and Saudi Arabia

· Civil 3D design skills, pipe and pressure networks

· Corridor and rainbow corridor modelling

· BIM standards and model management, including data shortcuts

· Design collaboration and the common data environment

· Clash detection and coordination

· Utility compliance verification, depth and cover against authority standards

· Quality assurance and technical awareness

title: Production Technologist
location: Jalan Tun Razak, Wilayah Persekutuan Kuala Lumpur
description:
Role Summary:

We are seeking a skilled and experienced Production Technologist to join our dynamic team in the oil and gas industry. As a Production Technologist, you’ll provide overall leadership, vision, and direction for a comprehensive alliance team. You will be responsible for optimizing and maximizing the production of oil wells through effective well design, production techniques, and reservoir management. Your expertise will contribute to the overall success of our operations, ensuring efficient and cost-effective production processes. You will collaborate with cross-functional teams, including other engineers, geologists, and field operators, to develop and execute production strategies that maximize reservoir performance and deliver consistent results.

Essential Responsibilities:

  • Being recognized internally and externally as an expert in production technology disciplines. Well Design and Operation.
  • Collaborate with other discipline engineers to design and implement well completion and production plans, including well completion, artificial lift systems, stimulation, and
  • workover activities, to optimize production rates.

Production Optimization:

  • Evaluate and optimize production strategies, monitor well performance, and identify
  • opportunities to enhance productivity and efficiency.
  • Implement and manage production enhancement techniques to improve well productivity and optimize reservoir recovery.
  • Analyse well performance data, including production rates, pressures, and fluid
  • properties, to identify production inefficiencies and propose remedial measures.
  • Conduct regular well reviews and performance evaluations to identify opportunities for
  • production optimization and implement appropriate actions.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to troubleshoot production issues and
  • recommend solutions to maximize well production and minimize downtime.
  • Leading projects of significant size and complexity as well as identify areas for
  • operational improvement and cost optimization, propose solutions, and implement best
  • practices to enhance production efficiency.
  • undefined

Reservoir Management


  • Support reservoir characterization and modelling efforts by providing technical inputs on well performance and production data.
  • Monitor reservoir behavior and perform analysis to identify reservoir depletion trends and potential production risks.
  • Collaborate with reservoir engineers to develop reservoir management strategies, including well spacing, artificial lift methods, and fluid injection programs.
  • Participate in reservoir management meetings and contribute to the development of long-term production plans and forecasts.

HSE


  • Ensure compliance with applicable industry regulations, company policies, and safetystandards in all production activities.
  • Participate in safety audits, risk assessments, and incident investigations to promote asafe working environment.
  • Implement appropriate measures to minimize environmental impacts associated with production operations.
  • Stay updated with industry trends, technological advancements, and best practicesrelated to production optimization and reservoir management.
  • Providing mentoring and training activities to junior petroleum engineers in the alliance team, fostering a culture of continuous learning and development.
  • Stay updated with the latest technologies, tools, and industry trends to identify opportunities for technological advancements and recommend their implementation for improved production processes.
  • Communicating effectively with other functional areas required and influencing peers to meet business objectives

Qualifications/Requirements:

  • Have a Bachelor's degree in Petroleum Engineering, Chemical Engineering, or a relateddiscipline with a minimum of 10+ years of relevant experience.
  • Proven experience working as a Production Technologist in the oil and gas industry, with a strong understanding of well design, production optimization, well performance analysis, and reservoir management.
  • Proficient in the use of industry-specific software and tools for reservoir modelling, production forecasting, and well performance analysis.
  • Familiarity with artificial lift systems, well completions, and surface facility operations.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to interpret complex data sets and make informed decisions.
  • Have demonstrate effective communication, interpersonal and leadership skills with the ability to mentor others as well as the ability to collaborate effectively with cross-functional teams.
  • Be a good team player and display good communication skills.
  • Knowledge of industry regulations, safety standards, and environmental practices relevant to oil and gas production.
  • Ability to adapt to changing priorities, work under pressure, and deliver high-quality results within tight deadlines.
  • Adherence to HSE regulations and a commitment to promoting a safe work environment.

Desired Characteristics:

Proficient in production software (e.g., Prosper, GAP, MBAL, WinGlue, NETool).

title: Applied Science III
description:
Do you want to make AI provably correct for chip design and verification? We're hiring an Applied Scientist to combine large language models with formal methods such as Lean 4 and turn AI from a helpful assistant into a trusted engineering tool for silicon.

Our team builds the formal verification methods behind custom silicon at Amazon scale. As AI agents take on more of chip design and verification, we need people who can make sure their output is checkable, sound and grounded in mathematics. You will research and build systems where LLMs work alongside interactive theorem provers, SMT solvers and model checkers. Engineers write the specifications. AI refines them against RTL, generates proof steps and closes proofs at machine speed. Every result is checked by a formal kernel, not trusted on faith.

Work at the frontier of AI reasoning, theorem proving and hardware verification
Ship solutions that directly affect real chips running in AWS data centers
Publish and help shape how the industry formalizes AI use in hardware engineering

Key job responsibilities
Design and build LLM-driven systems for formal verification and design tasks, including proof generation, invariant and lemma discovery, spec-to-RTL refinement, and counterexample analysis
Develop frameworks in Lean 4 (and related tools such as SMT solvers, model checkers and commercial FV engines) that formally check AI-generated artifacts, so they are correct by construction rather than just plausible
Formalize hardware semantics, ISAs and microarchitectural properties in Lean 4 to create machine-checkable foundations for AI agents to reason over
Track and evaluate state-of-the-art AI work (LLM agents, autoformalization, neural theorem proving, reinforcement learning from proof feedback) and turn promising research into production tools
Build benchmarks and evaluation methods that measure AI soundness, proof success rate and engineering impact on real designs
Partner with FV and design engineers to find the highest-leverage problems and deploy solutions into active chip programs
Publish research, file patents and represent Amazon in the formal methods and AI communities
Mentor engineers and scientists on applying formal AI methods

Berlin | Full-Time | Start ASAP

We're looking for an exceptional engineer. A true A-player who wants to take ownership, build world-class technology, and play a key role in shaping the future of Heidi Systems.

About Heidi Systems

Submetering in Germany still runs mostly on paper. Meters get read by hand, data sits in PDFs, and tenants see their consumption once a year.

Heidi Systems changes that end to end. We install meters and gateways in buildings, collect the data and build the platform property managers use to monitor consumption and run the yearly utility billing.

We have paying customers, a growing pipeline and an angel round with unicorn founders and directors from Google and OpenAI. Now we need an engineer who can carry a big part of the technical foundation together with the founders.

The role

You'll be one of the technical leads at Heidi and work directly with the founders. You make the architecture decisions, build them yourself and run them in production.

As the team grows, you'll help hire and mentor the next engineers.

What you'll own

  • Backend services in Go and TypeScript, including the API our SvelteKit frontend talks to

  • Microservices: deciding where to split services and building them, mostly in Go

  • Data pipelines: ingestion, validation and processing of meter, gateway and building data. These numbers end up on invoices, so they have to be right.

  • Databases and storage: PostgreSQL, Supabase and S3. Schema design, performance, backups, replication.

  • IoT and connectivity: MQTT, message brokers, wireless gateways and the bugs that only show up with real hardware in a basement

  • Infrastructure and deployments: Hetzner servers, Docker, Caddy, GitHub Actions, GHCR

  • Monitoring and incidents: logging, alerting and a clear process for when something breaks

  • Engineering standards: code review, testing and how we ship

What you bring

title: Events & Community Lead
description:

We're a veteran team of product builders and operators (formerly Google, Microsoft, and Apple). Our business is growing rapidly, and we're backed by leading investors including Y Combinator and founders of Dropbox, Instacart, Optimizely, and Gusto.

Location: San Francisco, CA (hybrid) · Type: Full-time · Reports to: CEO

About the role

Events are how most people will first meet Voicepanel. Community is why they stay connected. You’ll own both: running our events in person and online, and building a community of research, product, and marketing leaders who look forward to every gathering we host.

This is a focused role: no SEO, blog, or paid ads. Your job is to build an events program and community that create real relationships and turn them into customers. You’ll get real ownership, a direct line to our founders, and the backing to do this well.

title: Software Development Engineer II - Change Review , Amazon Software Builder Experience – Change Auto Review Experience (CRUX)
description:
Are you passionate about shaping the change review experience in the era of AI? The Change Review team within Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) builds the tools and services that help Amazon engineering teams understand, review, and ship software changes safely and confidently.

AI-assisted development is changing how software is created. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build the next generation of change-review tooling for this evolving environment. You will independently own substantial services, experiences, and integrations that make review workflows safer, clearer, and more efficient as engineers adopt new ways to build software.

In this role, you will work backwards from builders, define component designs where the customer problem or technical direction is known but the solution is not, and deliver reliable systems across their full lifecycle. You will exercise sound engineering judgment, make pragmatic trade-offs, influence technical decisions, and remain accountable for the quality and operation of what you build.

Key job responsibilities
- Independently own substantial features and components of developer-facing review tools, from customer discovery and scoping through design, implementation, validation, deployment, operations, and improvement.
- Work with builders, product managers, and partner teams to understand evolving software-development workflows and translate their needs into clear requirements and technical solutions.
- Design reliable services, interfaces, and experiences that help engineering teams review software changes, understand relevant signals, and take appropriate action.
- Build integrations with code-analysis, testing, source-control, and developer-workflow systems, accounting for downstream effects in related systems.
- Evaluate how emerging technologies, including AI-assisted development, change the needs and constraints of code-review systems, and recommend appropriate technical approaches.
- Make and explain trade-offs across customer experience, business priorities, delivery speed, operational work, security, scalability, and long-term architectural health.
- Remain accountable for the correctness, security, maintainability, performance, test coverage, and operational readiness of the software you deliver, regardless of the tools used to produce it.
- Own operational health, diagnose root causes, deliver durable corrections, reduce systemic support costs, and improve reliability, observability, and technical processes.
- Lead constructive technical and design reviews, align with partner teams, share knowledge, and mentor less-experienced engineers.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a design discussion, whiteboarding a new feature with your team before diving into hands-on coding. You will balance building new capabilities with improving existing systems, participating in code reviews, and sharing knowledge with teammates. You will regularly connect with product partners to ensure what you are building aligns with customer needs, and you will have the autonomy to propose and experiment with new approaches that make your team's software better.

About the team
Our team is focused on building software that directly impacts the customer experience at Amazon. We value collaboration, technical craftsmanship, and a commitment to operational excellence. We invest in each other's growth through mentorship, knowledge sharing, and an inclusive environment where every voice is heard. As we look ahead, we are excited about opportunities to apply new technologies and simplify our systems to deliver even greater value for our customers.

title: Field Business Management, Assistant Vice President

description:
Morgan Stanley is a leading global financial services firm providing a wide range of investment banking, securities, investment management and wealth management services. The Firm's employees serve clients worldwide including corporations, governments, and individuals from more than 1,200 offices in 43 countries.


As a market leader, the talent and passion of our people is critical to our success. Together, we share a common set of values rooted in integrity, excellence, and strong team ethic. Morgan Stanley can provide a superior foundation for building a professional career - a place for people to learn, to achieve and grow. A philosophy that balances personal lifestyles, perspectives and needs is an important part of our culture.



The Field Management division consists of Morgan Stanley’s network of ~16K Financial Advisors across ~510 branches representing $9.3T in client assets. The group is responsible for acquiring new assets for the firm’s full-service Wealth Management business, managing client relationships, and driving initiatives related to increasing the breadth of client relationships.


The Division is split between Wealth Management Field and Field Management Home Office (Corporate Management team). The Field Management Home Office internal “corporate” team is responsible for managing and driving strategic initiatives for the broader Wealth Management Field organization; its various teams include Field CAO, Business Development and Field Training, Private & International Wealth Management, Field Business Risk and Field Business Management.


Field Business Management (“FBM”) reports directly to the Head of Field Management and is focused on partnering with the Field leadership team and other senior members of Wealth Management to analyze, define, drive, and manage the top strategic priorities of the organization. The team’s responsibilities are split across five verticals: 1) FA Compensation Policy & Program Management, 2) Manager Compensation Policy & Program Management, 3) Advisor Legacy Program Policy & Program Management, 4) Advisor Retention and 5) Advisor Recruiting.




Position Summary:



The Field Business Management Assistant Vice President (AVP) will play a strategic role on the Advisor Legacy Program (ALP) Policy team within the FBM organization. The Advisor Legacy Program is a key component of Morgan Stanley’s approach to Advisor succession, providing a structured framework for experienced Financial Advisors to transition their practices and client relationships to successor Financial Advisors as they move toward retirement. The program is designed to support thoughtful succession planning, continuity of client relationships and practices, and an orderly transition of an Advisor’s business, while providing a defined economic framework for participating Advisors and successor teams.


Given the importance of Advisor succession to the long-term health of the Wealth Management franchise, the ALP team partners closely with Field leadership and senior management to oversee the program, evolve its policy and economics, and support its execution across the Field.


The AVP will help drive and manage key components of the Advisor Legacy Program, combining strategy, policy management, financial analysis, program execution and cross-functional partnership.




Key responsibilities include:



  • Comprehensive Policy Understanding: Develop an in-depth understanding of the Advisor Legacy Program Policy to effectively support Field and Home Office Leadership in execution of the program.
  • Collaboration with Field: Partner with the Field Management leadership team to deliver program / policy changes across the Field organization. Manage Field inquiries from both Advisors and Managers and assist with deal valuations / enrollment execution, including award valuation model-building.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration: Act as a liaison with Risk, Legal, Technology and other cross-functional teams to facilitate the strategic execution of the program, ensuring alignment with organizational goals. Partner closely with Legal on policy developments and their impact on the program.
  • Advanced Visualization & Presentation: Utilize advanced PowerPoint skills to create refined, visually compelling presentations for senior management and the Field, ensuring clear communication of complex data.
  • Analytical Excellence: Develop analytics from multiple streams of data, interpret and analyze trends, develop actionable insights and provide strategic recommendations for senior management. Modernize program analytics and KPI management by automating recurring reporting and building scalable dashboards. Manage basic expense tracking, advanced forecasting and accounting policy development, including the modeling of various scenarios and resulting impact on program P&L. Basic proficiency with Excel is required; statistical knowledge is encouraged.
  • Project Management: Apply strong process and project-management skills to manage multiple projects simultaneously, reprioritize as needed and solve problems autonomously.
  • Process Improvement Leadership: Define and implement detailed process improvements, monitoring progress across key annual deliverables to ensure continuous enhancement of program efficiency. Manage control processes related to business operations and audit preparedness.
  • AI Integration: Create and manage existing AI Agents for the ALP Program, delivering innovative solutions that drive scalable efficiency.



Qualifications and Education Requirements:



  • 3-5 years of relevant experience, with significant exposure to Wealth Management
  • Bachelor’s degree in business or a related field preferred, with a strong academic record
  • Must possess Financial Services industry experience and knowledge of industry trends and competitive advantages
  • Strong strategic planning, finance, conceptual design, collaborative, and organizational skills
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills, including presentation capabilities
  • Advanced proficiency in MS Excel, PowerPoint, Word, and Adobe PDF
  • Familiarity with Dataiku and various AI language models is a plus



Preferred Skills:



  • A proactive learner with a positive attitude, comfortable meeting established deadlines across diverse functional areas
  • Demonstrated self-starter with the ability to thrive in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment
  • Strategic thinker with the ability to align insights with firm strategy
  • Strong process management skills, with attention to detail and a commitment to meeting deadlines
  • Motivation for continuous improvement and innovation
  • Exceptional listening skills, with the ability to craft executive-level presentations
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced and dynamic environment; resilience under pressure and flexibility

WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY:

At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work.

To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices​ into your browser.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Procurement Lifecycle
description:
Procurement Lifecycle owns the software systems that generate purchase orders to procure hundreds of billions of dollars' worth of retail inventory each year. It's important that we reliably create, store, update, and convey purchase orders to thousands of vendors, helping to ensure that Amazon will have the products in stock that our customers want and love.

As the team's Technical Program Manager III, you will own the development of Inbound Instructions: a complex, multi-organization initiative to change how Amazon orders and merchandises retail inventory. Inbound Instructions will drive $1.9B in incremental GMS while simplifying purchase order processing and inbound operations. In the longer term, you will analyze current software systems, "look around corners" and anticipate future customer needs, and develop and execute a multi-year plan to improve the architecture, capabilities, performance, and efficiency of Inbound Instructions and other sourcing and operational systems.

In your role, you will collaborate with engineering managers, senior engineers, and senior product managers across Amazon Stores teams to drive the rollout of Inbound Instructions, manage 1–3-year roadmaps, and produce results. As part of Amazon's annual planning process (OP1/OP2), you will contribute to the development of technical and business goals. You will be accountable for the development lifecycle process, ensuring that deliverables and goals are met, while also contributing to the daily operational needs of the business.

You should be comfortable designing high-level architecture for software systems, but also be able to deep dive into low-level details. You should be able to suggest and carry out practical actions to deal with urgent issues while also managing the design and implementation of highly available, high-throughput software systems to address the long-term needs of the business. To excel in this role, it is also necessary to have strong written and verbal communication skills, business acumen, and an ability to effectively communicate customer and product requirements. As the owner of critical systems that impact a broad audience, you will need to be able to drive alignment among internal stakeholders who often have conflicting requirements or priorities.

Ready to own the engine that will force-multiply Amazon's access to inventory supply? Step into a role where your decisions ripple across the global supply chain, drive $1.9B in new sales, and shape how the world's most customer-obsessed company sources the products its customers love. Apply today and build what's next!

title: Software Development Engineer II - Change Review , Amazon Software Builder Experience – Change Auto Review Experience (CRUX)
description:
Are you passionate about shaping the change review experience in the era of AI? The Change Review team within Amazon Software Builder Experience (ASBX) builds the tools and services that help Amazon engineering teams understand, review, and ship software changes safely and confidently.

AI-assisted development is changing how software is created. We are looking for a Software Development Engineer II to build the next generation of change-review tooling for this evolving environment. You will independently own substantial services, experiences, and integrations that make review workflows safer, clearer, and more efficient as engineers adopt new ways to build software.

In this role, you will work backwards from builders, define component designs where the customer problem or technical direction is known but the solution is not, and deliver reliable systems across their full lifecycle. You will exercise sound engineering judgment, make pragmatic trade-offs, influence technical decisions, and remain accountable for the quality and operation of what you build.

Key job responsibilities
- Independently own substantial features and components of developer-facing review tools, from customer discovery and scoping through design, implementation, validation, deployment, operations, and improvement.
- Work with builders, product managers, and partner teams to understand evolving software-development workflows and translate their needs into clear requirements and technical solutions.
- Design reliable services, interfaces, and experiences that help engineering teams review software changes, understand relevant signals, and take appropriate action.
- Build integrations with code-analysis, testing, source-control, and developer-workflow systems, accounting for downstream effects in related systems.
- Evaluate how emerging technologies, including AI-assisted development, change the needs and constraints of code-review systems, and recommend appropriate technical approaches.
- Make and explain trade-offs across customer experience, business priorities, delivery speed, operational work, security, scalability, and long-term architectural health.
- Remain accountable for the correctness, security, maintainability, performance, test coverage, and operational readiness of the software you deliver, regardless of the tools used to produce it.
- Own operational health, diagnose root causes, deliver durable corrections, reduce systemic support costs, and improve reliability, observability, and technical processes.
- Lead constructive technical and design reviews, align with partner teams, share knowledge, and mentor less-experienced engineers.

A day in the life
Your morning might start with a design discussion, whiteboarding a new feature with your team before diving into hands-on coding. You will balance building new capabilities with improving existing systems, participating in code reviews, and sharing knowledge with teammates. You will regularly connect with product partners to ensure what you are building aligns with customer needs, and you will have the autonomy to propose and experiment with new approaches that make your team's software better.

About the team
Our team is focused on building software that directly impacts the customer experience at Amazon. We value collaboration, technical craftsmanship, and a commitment to operational excellence. We invest in each other's growth through mentorship, knowledge sharing, and an inclusive environment where every voice is heard. As we look ahead, we are excited about opportunities to apply new technologies and simplify our systems to deliver even greater value for our customers.

title: Software Development Engineer, Region Services
description:
Applicants must be Australian citizens and hold or be eligible to obtain an Australian Government Security Clearance with the ability to successfully complete an Organisational Suitability Assessment. For more information regarding security clearances please visit (https://www.agsva.gov.au/).

AWS Region Services is responsible for building and operating the foundational infrastructure that powers AWS Regions across the globe. Our team designs, builds, and operates large-scale distributed systems that millions of customers depend on every day for compute, storage, security, and data management workloads.

We are looking for Software Development Engineers to join our team in Melbourne and help expand and strengthen AWS's regional infrastructure in Australia. You will design, implement, and operate distributed services that handle critical workloads at AWS scale. You will own features end-to-end, from design and implementation through testing, deployment, and production operations. You will work with junior engineers providing mentoring, and senior engineers designing and planning software solutions to complex problems.

You will work in an agile environment alongside other experienced developers and engineers, tackling problems in areas such as large-scale automation, service reliability, and cross-region operations. If you want your engineering decisions to have real impact at AWS scale, we would love to hear from you.

These roles are strictly Melbourne based, however we will provide interstate relocation support.

Key job responsibilities
- Design, implement, and operate distributed services and tooling that support AWS regional infrastructure at scale.
- Own features end-to-end, from scoping and design through coding, testing, deployment, and live-site operations.
- Contribute to system architecture decisions, balancing trade-offs between scalability, performance, availability, and cost.
- Collaborate with engineers across multiple teams and AWS organisations to deliver cross-service integrations and platform improvements.
- Write clean, well-tested, maintainable code and raise the engineering bar through thoughtful code reviews and design discussions.
- Drive improvements including performance optimisations, infrastructure modernisation, and technical debt reduction.
- Participate in on-call rotations to ensure service reliability and drive root-cause fixes for production issues.
- Mentor fellow engineers and contribute to a team culture of continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and inclusion.

A day in the life
No two days look the same. You might spend the morning designing a new automation capability, the afternoon debugging a latency issue across a distributed system and end the day reviewing a teammate's design document. You will work with engineers across your team and across AWS to solve problems that do not always have clear answers, from building customer-facing features to optimising system performance to delivering cross-team integrations. We value engineers who are curious, pragmatic, and comfortable with ambiguity. You will have real ownership from day one.

About the team
Diverse Experiences
Amazon values diverse experiences. Even if you do not meet all the preferred qualifications and skills listed in the job description, we encourage candidates to apply. If your career is just starting, hasn’t followed a traditional path, or includes alternative experiences, don’t let it stop you from applying.

Why AWS
Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses.

Work/Life Balance
We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we cannot achieve in the cloud.

Inclusive Team Culture
Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon (diversity) conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness.

Mentorship and Career Growth
We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

  • Provide input into project build estimates and coordinate technical requirements with relevant stakeholders.

  • At least five years of experience in middleware administration.

title: Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS Industries - Media & Entertainment, Games and Sports (AWSI-MEGS)
description:
Are you a hands-on technologist who loves solving complex customer problems? Do you enjoy working with engineering teams and technical leaders to design solutions that deliver real business results? If so, we want to hear from you.
As a Senior Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services (AWS), you'll partner with media and entertainment customers to design and deliver cloud solutions that are scalable, secure, cost-optimized and high-performing. You'll be the trusted technical advisor for your accounts, turning business requirements into practical architectures and guiding customers from early ideas through to production. Your technical depth, customer focus and clear communication will help organizations adopt AWS and succeed with it. Your customer insights will also help shape the AWS services that customers build on.

Key job responsibilities
• Own the technical relationship for a set of strategic customer accounts. Work backward from customer business goals to design end-to-end solutions that are extensible, secure, reliable and cost-optimized.
• Build trust with customer architects, engineering leaders and technical decision-makers. Understand their challenges and guide architecture decisions that support both near-term delivery and long-term goals.
• Lead deep technical discussions on design choices, best practices and the trade-offs between implementation options. Spot and reduce risks early, and steer customers away from approaches that are needlessly complex.
• Create and deliver technical content such as presentations, workshops, reference architectures and sample code that help customers apply AWS best practices.
• Work with account managers, professional services, partners, support and service teams to speed up adoption. Contribute reusable patterns and assets to the wider Solutions Architecture community.
• Build deep expertise in one or more media domains (streaming, media supply chain, ad tech) and in generative AI, and keep your knowledge current as the industry changes.
• Build and present hands-on prototypes, demos and proofs of concept that prove technical feasibility and speed up the path to production.
• Work with ISVs and industry partners to design and validate joint solutions across live streaming, media asset management, and ad delivery and personalization.
• Pass customer feedback and feature requests to AWS service teams so the product roadmap reflects what customers actually need.
• Share what you know through blogs, conference talks and community events, and mentor other SAs to grow technical depth across the team.

A day in the life
You might start your morning getting ready for an architecture review with a streaming customer's engineering leads. You'd look over their current video delivery setup and find places where AWS services could improve scale, resilience or cost. Mid-morning, you could be at the whiteboard with their developers, designing a live-event workflow and weighing the trade-offs between reliability, latency and cost. After lunch, you might be hands-on building a generative AI proof of concept that automates metadata tagging for a media asset library. Later, you'd meet with your account manager to plan next steps for the customer. You might finish the day by writing up a feature request for an AWS service team based on what you heard from customers, or by reviewing a reference architecture with a fellow SA you're mentoring.

About the team
We're the AWS Media, Entertainment, Games and Sports (MEGS) Solutions Architecture team, and our vision is simple: we meet our customers where they are, design what's next, prove what's possible, and scale what matters for every fan, every story, every screen, and every experience. #InventForFans

We come with a point of view, staying on the frontier of technology and pushing it where it matters most to our customers. We're builders who roll up our sleeves to create demos, proofs of concept, and prototypes, because a working idea beats a slide every time. We collaborate across account teams, specialists, and service teams, acting as the connective tissue that shapes what gets built next. And we scale our thinking, turning what we learn in the field into patterns and reference architectures that the whole industry can use. Every activity backs an outcome for our customers, and we're intentional about the work that matters.
